title: Empowerment of Women and other Weaker Sections

facts.text: In 1972, under the leadership of the socialist leader Mrinal Gore, women in Mumbai took part in the laatne morcha (the rolling pin demonstration).
facts.quote: Women, who have to face the brunt of scarcity of supplies and rising prices, gave a show of their strength as an organised entity in 1972. Under the leadership of the socialist leader Mrinal Gore, women in Mumbai participated in a demonstration which came to be known as the laatne morcha (the rolling pin demonstration).

facts.text: Oil, ghee, rava and maida became scarce just as Diwali was near and kerosene was very expensive; women brandished rolling pins and the movement met with success.
facts.quote: Commodities like oil, ghee, rava, maida, would become scarce just as Diwali was near at hand. Kerosene had become very expensive. Women came together brandishing their rolling pins and took part in the demonstration. This movement met with success

facts.text: The Chipko movement of 1973: trees in the foothills of the Himalayas were to be cut down for commercial purposes; Chandiprasad Bhat and Sunderlal Bahuguna started a movement to prevent this.
facts.quote: Another show of constructive woman power was seen during the Chipko movement in 1973. Trees from the forests in the foothills of the Himalayas were to be cut down for commercial purposes. Chandiprasad Bhat and Sunderlal Bahuguna had started a movement to prevent this.

facts.text: Women held hands and encircled each tree; as they protected a tree by embracing it, the movement came to be known as the Chipko movement.
facts.quote: Women followed the strategy of holding hands and encircling each tree. As their method consisted of protecting the tree by embracing it, the movement came to be known as the Chipko movement.

facts.text: Gaura Devi was the activist who created awareness among the women in the Chipko movement with the help of Sudesha Devi and Bachani Devi.
facts.quote: Gaura Devi was the activist who created this awareness among the women with the help of Sudesha Devi and Bachani Devi.

facts.text: Vinoba Bhave made use of woman power in the Bhoodan Movement, which he started placing his faith in Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy; women volunteers carried its message to all parts of India.
facts.quote: Vinoba Bhave made use of woman power in the Bhoodan Movement which he had started placing his faith in Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy. Women volunteers carried the message of Bhoodan to all parts of India.

facts.text: Women played a significant role in the Telangana Peasants Armed Struggle, which challenged the rule of the nizams and the feudal system.
facts.quote: Women played a significant role in the Telangana Peasants Armed Struggle which challenged the rule of the nizams and the feudal system. As their region became free from bonded labour, women also found freedom from this torment.

facts.text: In 1992 a movement against the drinking of alcohol was started in Andhra Pradesh; it got the support of the anti-arrack movement.
facts.quote: In 1992, in Andhra Pradesh, a movement was started against the drinking of alcohol. ... This movement got the support of the anti-arrack movement in Andhra Pradesh.

facts.text: Arrack is a locally produced alcohol; as a result of a government policy, arrack dealers set up shop in every town and village.
facts.quote: As a result of a government policy, arrack (a locally produced alcohol) dealers set up shop in every town and village.

facts.text: The Sitama Katha (Sita's story), narrated in a literacy programme, was about Sita who creates awareness among the people of a village and gets alcohol banned from the village.
facts.quote: The Sitama Katha (Sita's story) was narrated as a part of this programme. It was a story about Sita who creates awareness among the people of a village and gets alcohol to be banned from the village.

facts.text: In 1992 three youths of Dubuganta village of Nellore district in Andhra Pradesh drowned in a lake; the women of the village forced the closure of arrack shops and the movement spread to the entire State.
facts.quote: In 1992, three youths of Dubuganta village of Nellore district in Andhra Pradesh drowned in a lake, in a state of inebriation, and died. At this instance, the women of the village came together and forced the closure of arrack shops. ... The movement spread to the entire State and the government had to adopt a strict policy against the sale of alcohol.

facts.text: The United Nations declared 1975 as the International Women's Year; its three aspects were peace, development and equality between men and women.
facts.quote: The United Nations had declared 1975 as the International Women's Year. The three aspects of this programme were peace, development and equality between men and women.

facts.text: In 1975 the government of India constituted the Committee on the Status of Women and appointed Dr Phulrenu Guha as its Chairman; it surveyed issues such as wages, education and the female-male ratio.
facts.quote: In 1975, the government of India constituted the Committee on the Status of Women and appointed Dr Phulrenu Guha as its Chairman. A comprehensive survey was conducted of several issues such as ... their wages (relative to men's wages), the female-male ratio

facts.text: In 1975 a State-wide conference for women was organised by the Stree-mukti Sangharsha Samiti.
facts.quote: a State-wide conference for women was held in 1975 organised by the Stree-mukti Sangharsha Samiti.

facts.text: The Stree-mukti Sangharsha Samiti published its manifesto in 1978, adopting a struggle against discrimination on the basis of gender, caste and varna.
facts.quote: The Samiti published its manifesto in 1978. The policy of a struggle against discrimination on the basis of gender, caste and varna was adopted.

facts.text: This gave rise to the song collection Streemuktichi Lalkari, the street play Mulgi Jhaali Ho by Jyoti Mhapsekar and the periodical Prerak Lalkari, their mouthpiece.
facts.quote: This gave rise to a collection of songs called Streemuktichi Lalkari, a street play called Mulgi Jhaali Ho by Jyoti Mhapsekar and a periodical called Prerak Lalkari which became their mouthpiece

facts.text: In 1977 groups like the Streemukti Andolan Samiti established by Soudamini Rao in Pune and Bayaja, a fortnightly, were formed.
facts.quote: In 1977, groups like the Streemukti Andolan Samiti established by Soudamini Rao in Pune, Bayaja a fortnightly

facts.text: Mahila Dakshata Samiti in Kolhapur, Mahila Hakka in Nashik and Nari Prabodhan Manch in Latur were also formed.
facts.quote: Mahila Dakshata Samiti in Kolhapur, Mahila Hakka in Nashik and Nari Prabodhan Manch in Latur were formed.

facts.text: Anti-dowry protection committees were formed all over Maharashtra, and a conference to protest against oppression of women was organised in Dhule city.
facts.quote: Anti-dowry protection committees were formed all over Maharashtra. A conference to protest against oppression of women was organised in Dhule city.

facts.text: Vidya Bal's periodicals Nari Samata Manch and Milun Saryajani, and the work of the Samajwadi Mahila Sabha and the Krantikari Mahila Sanghatana helped in dealing with women's issues.
facts.quote: Vidya Bal's periodicals, Nari Samata Manch, and Milun Saryajani, as also the work of the Samajwadi Mahila Sabha and the Krantikari Mahila Sanghatana were of great help in dealing with women's issues.

facts.text: The Employment Guarantee Scheme in Maharashtra also helped to empower women.
facts.quote: The Employment Guarantee Scheme in Maharashtra also helped to empower women.

facts.text: Pramila Dandavate established the Mahila Dakshata Samiti in Delhi in 1976; branches came up in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.
facts.quote: Pramila Dandavate established the Mahila Dakshata Samiti in Delhi in 1976. Branches of the Samiti came up in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

facts.text: The Communist Party established the Akhil Bharatiya Janavadi Mahila Sanghatana in 1980; it struggled against dowry, female foeticide and domestic abuse.
facts.quote: The Communist Party established the Akhil Bharatiya Janavadi Mahila Sanghatana in 1980. ... The Sanghatana started a struggle against issues like dowry, female foeticide, domestic abuse.

facts.text: Women's Studies Centres were started at SNDT Women's University (the first women's university) Mumbai, Tata Institute of Social Sciences Mumbai, Savitribai Phule Pune University and Shivaji University Kolhapur.
facts.quote: Women's Studies Centres were started at the first women's university, the Shrimati Nathibai Damodar Thakersey (SNDT) Women's University, Mumbai, and at Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai, Savitribai Phule Pune University, Pune and Shivaji University, Kolhapur.

facts.text: The law enacted in 1952 recognised women's right to alimony, a share in the father's property and streedhan; polygamy was made illegal and women got the right to sue for divorce.
facts.quote: The law enacted in 1952, recognises women's right to alimony and their share in the father's property. Her right to streedhan was recognised. Polygamy was made illegal and women, just like men, got the right to sue for divorce.

facts.text: The Dowry Prohibition Act of 1961 made both giving and taking of dowry a cognizable criminal offence.
facts.quote: The Dowry Prohibition Act of 1961 made both giving and taking of dowry a cognizable criminal offence.

facts.text: The Maternity Benefit Act, giving women leave from work at the time of child-birth, came into force in 1961.
facts.quote: The Maternity Benefit Act which gave women the right to get leave from work at the time of child-birth also came into force in 1961.

facts.text: As a result of greater awareness, the Dowry Prohibition (Amendment) Act came into force in 1984.
facts.quote: This created greater awareness. As a result, the Dowry Prohibition (Amendment) Act came into force in 1984.

facts.text: Family Courts (1984) resolve family conflicts such as alimony, separation and care of children, giving priority to mutual understanding over witnesses and evidence and to counsellors over lawyers.
facts.quote: Family Courts (1984) : Family courts were established to resolve conflicts arising out of differences within marriage and domestic problems as well as issues such as alimony, single parenthood, separation, care of children and ownership ... These family courts give priority to mutual understanding over witnesses and evidence and to counsellors over lawyers.

facts.text: Alimony is a fixed amount paid to a married woman for her upkeep by the husband who has divorced her.
facts.quote: A fixed amount paid to a married woman for her upkeep by the husband who has divorced her, is called alimony.

facts.text: Trial involving alimony (1985): in Mohammad Ahmed Khan vs Shah Bano Begum the Supreme Court ruled that Shah Bano Begum had the right to alimony; after protests, Parliament passed the 'Muslim Women's Act'.
facts.quote: Trial involving alimony (1985) : ... In the case of Mohammad Ahmed Khan vs Shah Bano Begum, the Supreme Court gave the verdict that Shah Bano Begum had the right to alimony. However, religious organisations protested vociferously against the verdict. As a result, the 'Muslim Women's Act' (Protection of rights on divorce) was passed by Parliament.

facts.text: On 4th September 1987 Roop Kanwar, a married woman, was coerced into committing sati.
facts.quote: On 4th September 1987, Roop Kanwar, a married woman, committed sati. She did not do this of her own free will; she was coerced into doing so.

facts.text: Women activists and journalists Meena Menon, Geeta Seshu, Sujata Anandan, Anu Joseph and Kalpana Sharma investigated the Roop Kanwar case.
facts.quote: The women activists and journalists, Meena Menon, Geeta Seshu, Sujata Anandan, Anu Joseph and Kalpana Sharma investigated the case.

facts.text: In 1988 the government passed the Sati (Prevention) Act with very stringent provisions.
facts.quote: In 1988, the government passed the Sati (Prevention) Act with very stringent provisions.

facts.text: The Protection of Human Rights Act was enacted in 1993; the National Human Rights Commission was formed, and in some States a State Human Rights Commission.
facts.quote: In 1993, this law was enacted to prevent injustice to men and women. The National Human Rights Commission was also formed for this purpose. In some States, the State Human Rights Commission was also formed on the same lines.

facts.text: The 73rd and 74th amendments to the Constitution reserve one-third of the seats for women in Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis, Zilla Parishads, municipalities and municipal corporations and for posts of Sarpanch, Chairman and Mayor.
facts.quote: The 73rd and 74th amendments to the Constitution provide for reservation of one-third of the seats for women in Gram Panchayats, Panchayat Samitis, Zilla Parishads, municipalities and municipal corporations as well as for the posts of Sarpanch, Chairman and Mayor.

facts.text: After independence the Constitution accepted the equality of men and women: women got the right to vote, and sati, dowry and polygamy were banned by law.
facts.quote: In the post-independence period, the Constitution of India accepted the principle of equality of men and women. Hence, women got the important political right to vote. ... Inhuman practices like sati, dowry and polygamy were banned by law.

facts.text: Women who have led their States as Chief Ministers include Sucheta Kripalani (Uttar Pradesh), Nandini Satpathy (Odisha), Sheila Dixit (Delhi) and Shashikala Kakodkar (Goa).
facts.quote: Sucheta Kripalani (Uttar Pradesh), Nandini Satpathy (Odisha), ... Sheila Dixit (Delhi), ... Shashikala Kakodkar (Goa), ... are all women who have led their States as Chief Ministers.

facts.text: On 8 March 1857 a demonstration in New York was the first demonstration by working women, demanding fewer working hours, proper remuneration and provision of creches.
facts.quote: A demonstration was held in New York on 8 March 1857. It was the first demonstration by working women and its demands were for fewer working hours, proper remuneration, provision of creches, etc.

facts.text: On 8 March 1909 women went on strike for the same demands; the day was declared Women's Struggle Day at the Women's Socialist International, a conference held in Denmark.
facts.quote: On 8 March 1909 women went on strike for the very same demands. That is why, this day was declared as the Women's Struggle Day at the Women's Socialist International, a conference held in Denmark.

facts.text: In 1977, 8 March was declared International Women's Day by a resolution of the General Assembly of the United Nations.
facts.quote: in 1977, 8 March was declared as International Women's Day by a resolution passed in the General Assembly of the United Nations.

facts.text: The Constitution adopted freedom, equality, fraternity and social justice; untouchability was removed by the 17th paragraph of the Constitution and Scheduled Castes were given reservations in education and jobs.
facts.quote: our Constitution adopted the values of freedom, equality, fraternity and social justice. ... Untouchability was removed by the 17th paragraph of the Constitution and this class was included in the Scheduled Castes. ... they were given reservations in education as well as jobs

facts.text: Adivasis, enumerated in the Constitution as Scheduled Tribes, live in remote parts, depend on agriculture and forest produce, and have fields on hillsides that are not fertile.
facts.quote: they do not have any means of livelihood other than agriculture and forest produce. ... their fields are on hillsides and not fertile. ... In the Indian Constitution, Adivasis have been enumerated as Scheduled Tribes.

facts.text: Nomadic Tribes move from place to place for a livelihood; under the Law of 1871 the British named some groups criminal tribes; after independence the law was repealed and they were included under De-notified Tribes.
facts.quote: Castes and tribes that move from place to place for a livelihood, are included under Nomadic Tribes. ... In the Law of 1871 to curb crimes, some of the main groups were mentioned as criminal tribes and their occupations and movements were banned. This unjust law was repealed in the post-independence period. ... They were included under De-notified Tribes.

facts.text: A minority is a group of people of a particular religion, language or race who are few in number; minorities have the right to set up separate educational institutions.
facts.quote: a group of people of a particular religion, language or race who are few in number are termed a minority. ... For this purpose they have the right to set up separate educational institutions.
